domains.applies_when: The content adds, changes or describes an HTTP endpoint, route, controller, request or response payload, or an API contract (OpenAPI).
domains.description: Design of HTTP/REST endpoints exposed by services, including paths, methods, status codes, errors, pagination and versioning.
domains.not_applies_when: No HTTP interface is added, changed or described.
domains.title: HTTP API design

domains.applies_when: The content adds or changes a database migration, a schema definition, DDL (CREATE/ALTER/DROP) or an ORM model mapped to a table.
domains.description: Changes to relational database schemas and the migrations that apply them.
domains.not_applies_when: No database schema or migration is added, changed or described.
domains.title: Database schema and migrations

domains.applies_when: The content adds, reads, changes or removes a feature flag, or changes user-visible behavior of a production service.
domains.description: How risky behavior changes are rolled out, including feature flags, flag ownership and cleanup.
domains.not_applies_when: No feature flag is involved and no user-visible production behavior changes.
domains.title: Safe delivery and feature flags

domains.applies_when: The content is an engineering standard, an RFC, or a change to the standards corpus.
domains.description: How engineering standards (jrfc RFCs) are written, reviewed and maintained.
domains.not_applies_when: Application code, product specs or docs that are not engineering standards.
domains.title: Standards governance

domains.applies_when: The content writes or configures logs, log messages, error messages, metrics, traces or telemetry.
domains.description: How services write logs, metrics and traces, and what data may appear in them.
domains.not_applies_when: No logging, metrics, tracing or telemetry is written or configured.
domains.title: Logging and observability

domains.applies_when: The content is or changes Python source code (.py files).
domains.description: Conventions for Python source code in services, jobs and tools.
domains.not_applies_when: The content is not Python source code.
domains.title: Python code

domains.applies_when: The content makes or configures an outbound network call (HTTP client, RPC, message broker, third-party SDK) or describes such a dependency.
domains.description: Timeouts, retries, backoff and failure handling for network calls to other services, databases or third parties.
domains.not_applies_when: No outbound network call is made, configured or described.
domains.title: Reliability of service-to-service calls

domains.applies_when: The content handles credentials, tokens, keys, user input, database queries, shell commands, authentication or authorization.
domains.description: Handling of secrets, credentials, untrusted input, queries and authentication in application code and designs.
domains.not_applies_when: The content is pure styling, copy text or documentation with no code that handles input, data or credentials.
domains.title: Application security

domains.applies_when: The content is a technical design document or spec that proposes how to build or change a system.
domains.description: The structure and completeness of technical design documents (specs, design docs, RFCs for systems) written before building.
domains.not_applies_when: The content is code, a diff, an incident report, or a doc that does not propose a system design.
domains.title: Technical design specs

domains.applies_when: The content is or changes TypeScript source code (.ts or .tsx files).
domains.description: Conventions for TypeScript source code in services and frontends.
domains.not_applies_when: The content is not TypeScript source code.
domains.title: TypeScript code

rfcs.applies_when: The content is a jrfc RFC file (front matter with an id like JRFC-0000) or a change to one.
rfcs.not_applies_when: Any content that is not a jrfc RFC file.
rfcs.summary: How a jrfc standard is structured so humans can read it and agents can select and enforce single statements from it.
rfcs.title: Format and lifecycle of jrfc standards

rfcs.applies_when: The content adds, changes or describes an HTTP endpoint, route, controller, handler, request/response payload or OpenAPI contract.
rfcs.not_applies_when: No HTTP endpoint or API contract is added, changed or described.
rfcs.summary: Conventions for HTTP endpoints: resource paths, methods, errors, pagination, idempotency and versioning.
rfcs.title: HTTP API design

rfcs.applies_when: The content writes log lines, error messages, traces or metric attributes, or configures a logger.
rfcs.not_applies_when: No logging, tracing, metrics or telemetry is written or configured.
rfcs.summary: How services write logs so that they are searchable, correlated and free of personal data.
rfcs.title: Logging and personal data

rfcs.applies_when: The content uses, stores, passes or describes a password, API key, token, private key, connection string or other credential.
rfcs.not_applies_when: No credential of any kind is used, stored, passed or described.
rfcs.summary: Where credentials, tokens and keys live and how code obtains and handles them.
rfcs.title: Secrets management

rfcs.applies_when: The content reads request parameters, bodies, headers, files or messages, or builds a database query, shell command, template or HTML from data.
rfcs.not_applies_when: The content does not read external input and does not build queries, commands or markup.
rfcs.summary: How code treats data that comes from users, clients or other systems, to prevent injection flaws (OWASP A03).
rfcs.title: Untrusted input and injection

rfcs.applies_when: The content makes, configures or describes an outbound network call: HTTP client, RPC, database driver, message broker or third-party SDK.
rfcs.not_applies_when: No outbound network call is made, configured or described.
rfcs.summary: Timeouts, retries and fallbacks for calls to other services, databases and third parties.
rfcs.title: Resilient outbound calls

rfcs.applies_when: The content is or changes TypeScript source code (.ts or .tsx).
rfcs.not_applies_when: The content is not TypeScript source code.
rfcs.summary: Type-safety and async conventions for TypeScript services and frontends.
rfcs.title: TypeScript code

rfcs.applies_when: The content adds or changes a database migration, DDL statement or schema definition.
rfcs.not_applies_when: No database schema or migration is involved.
rfcs.summary: How to change relational schemas without downtime, using the expand/contract pattern.
rfcs.title: Zero-downtime database migrations

rfcs.applies_when: The content is a technical design document or spec that proposes how to build or change a system.
rfcs.not_applies_when: The content is code, a diff, an incident report or a document that does not propose a system design.
rfcs.summary: The sections every technical design spec contains before implementation starts.
rfcs.title: Technical design specs

rfcs.applies_when: The content adds, reads, changes or removes a feature flag, or changes user-visible behavior of a production service.
rfcs.not_applies_when: No feature flag is involved and no user-visible production behavior changes.
rfcs.summary: When to put a change behind a feature flag and how flags are owned and removed.
rfcs.title: Feature flags

rfcs.applies_when: The content is or changes Python source code.
rfcs.not_applies_when: The content is not Python source code.
rfcs.summary: Draft proposal: type hints on public Python functions. Not used by agents until approved.
rfcs.title: Python type hints

statements.applies_when: the content adds or edits a `### JRFC-` statement heading or its text.
statements.not_applies_when: Any content that is not a jrfc RFC file.
statements.text: Each statement MUST use normative keywords of exactly one level (`MUST`/`SHALL`/`REQUIRED`, `SHOULD`/`RECOMMENDED`, or `MAY`/`OPTIONAL`); a statement that needs two levels is split in two.
statements.title: One normative level per statement

statements.applies_when: the content renames, removes or reorders `### JRFC-` statement headings.
statements.not_applies_when: Any content that is not a jrfc RFC file.
statements.text: A published statement identifier MUST NOT be renumbered or reused for a different requirement; a removed statement keeps its number retired.
statements.title: Stable statement identifiers

statements.applies_when: the content adds or edits a `### JRFC-` statement.
statements.not_applies_when: Any content that is not a jrfc RFC file.
statements.text: Each statement SHOULD have an `Applies when:` line that names the concrete code, text or situation it governs, written literally enough for a classifier to match.
statements.title: Explicit applicability

statements.applies_when: the content changes the `status:` field of an RFC front matter.
statements.not_applies_when: Any content that is not a jrfc RFC file.
statements.text: The `status` of an RFC MUST only move to `approved` or `enforced` with the approval of the domain owner; agents propose drafts and never promote them.
statements.title: Human approval of status

statements.applies_when: the content adds a statement about syntax, formatting, config flags or other mechanically checkable properties.
statements.not_applies_when: Any content that is not a jrfc RFC file.
statements.text: A statement that a linter or static check can verify exactly SHOULD be marked `Enforcement: linter` and implemented as a lint rule instead of an agent check.
statements.title: Mechanical rules go to linters

statements.applies_when: the content defines or changes an HTTP route path.
statements.not_applies_when: No HTTP endpoint or API contract is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Endpoint paths MUST name resources with plural nouns in kebab-case (for example `/booking-requests/{id}`) and MUST NOT contain verbs such as `get`, `create` or `update`.
statements.title: Resource-oriented paths

statements.applies_when: the content defines an HTTP handler and its method.
statements.not_applies_when: No HTTP endpoint or API contract is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Handlers MUST use HTTP methods according to RFC 9110: GET and HEAD MUST NOT change server state, and state changes use POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE.
statements.title: Methods match semantics

statements.applies_when: the content builds or returns an HTTP error response, or describes API errors.
statements.not_applies_when: No HTTP endpoint or API contract is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Error responses MUST use the `application/problem+json` format of RFC 9457 with at least `type`, `title` and `status`, and MUST NOT expose stack traces or internal exception text.
statements.title: Problem details for errors

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes an endpoint that returns a list or collection of items.
statements.not_applies_when: No HTTP endpoint or API contract is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Endpoints that return a collection MUST be paginated with a bounded maximum page size.
statements.title: Paginated collections

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a POST endpoint that creates a reservation, booking, payment, order or similar resource.
statements.not_applies_when: No HTTP endpoint or API contract is added, changed or described.
statements.text: POST endpoints that create reservations, payments or other resources with business side effects MUST accept an `Idempotency-Key` header and return the original result for a repeated key.
statements.title: Idempotent creation of money- or booking-related resources

statements.applies_when: the content removes or renames response fields, changes field types, or changes required request fields of an existing endpoint.
statements.not_applies_when: No HTTP endpoint or API contract is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A breaking change to a public API contract SHOULD be released as a new major version path (for example `/v2/`) while the previous version keeps working during a deprecation period.
statements.title: Versioning of breaking changes

statements.applies_when: a log, print, logger, span attribute or metric label call includes fields of a user, customer, guest, reservation or payment.
statements.not_applies_when: No logging, tracing, metrics or telemetry is written or configured.
statements.text: Services MUST NOT write personal data — names, email addresses, phone numbers, postal addresses, payment card data, or free-text messages written by customers — to logs, traces or metric attributes; use an opaque identifier such as the customer id instead.
statements.title: No personal data in logs

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a log call.
statements.not_applies_when: the content only changes logger configuration.
statements.text: Services MUST emit logs as structured key-value records through the shared logger, not as interpolated free-text strings built by concatenation.
statements.title: Structured logs

statements.applies_when: the content logs inside an HTTP handler, message consumer or job that processes a request or message.
statements.not_applies_when: No logging, tracing, metrics or telemetry is written or configured.
statements.text: Every log record written while handling a request or message MUST include the correlation id of that request or message.
statements.title: Correlation identifier

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a log call with a level.
statements.not_applies_when: No logging, tracing, metrics or telemetry is written or configured.
statements.text: Log levels SHOULD be used as follows: `error` for failures that need human action, `warn` for degraded but handled situations, `info` for business events, and `debug` for diagnostic detail that is off in production.
statements.title: Meaningful levels

statements.applies_when: the content contains a string literal, constant, config value or default that is or looks like a password, key, token or credential.
statements.not_applies_when: No credential of any kind is used, stored, passed or described.
statements.text: Source code, configuration files and tests MUST NOT contain real credentials (passwords, API keys, tokens, private keys, connection strings with passwords).
statements.title: No secrets in source

statements.applies_when: the content loads, configures or passes a credential for a database, broker, third-party API or service.
statements.not_applies_when: No credential of any kind is used, stored, passed or described.
statements.text: Services MUST read credentials at runtime from the secret manager (directly or through environment variables injected by the platform), never from files committed to the repository.
statements.title: Secrets from the secret manager

statements.applies_when: the content builds a URL, a log record or an error message in code that has access to a credential.
statements.not_applies_when: No credential of any kind is used, stored, passed or described.
statements.text: Credentials MUST NOT be placed in URL query strings, log records, error messages or exception text.
statements.title: Secrets never in URLs or logs

statements.applies_when: the content is a design that introduces a new credential, key or service account.
statements.not_applies_when: No credential of any kind is used, stored, passed or described.
statements.text: A design that introduces a new credential SHOULD describe how it is rotated and who owns the rotation.
statements.title: Rotation

statements.applies_when: the content builds or executes a SQL or NoSQL query.
statements.not_applies_when: The content does not read external input and does not build queries, commands or markup.
statements.text: Database queries MUST pass values as bound parameters (prepared statements or the ORM query builder) and MUST NOT build SQL by concatenating or interpolating values into the query string.
statements.title: Parameterized queries

statements.applies_when: the content reads request parameters, query strings, bodies or headers in a handler.
statements.not_applies_when: The content does not read external input and does not build queries, commands or markup.
statements.text: Request input MUST be validated against an explicit schema (types, required fields, lengths, allowed values) before it is used by business logic.
statements.title: Validate at the boundary

statements.applies_when: the content calls eval, exec, a subprocess or shell, or compiles a template.
statements.not_applies_when: The content does not read external input and does not build queries, commands or markup.
statements.text: Code MUST NOT pass untrusted input to `eval`, `Function`, `exec`, a shell, or a template compiler.
statements.title: No dynamic code or shell with input

statements.applies_when: the content creates an HTTP client, performs a fetch/request/RPC, or configures a client for another service or third party.
statements.not_applies_when: No outbound network call is made, configured or described.
statements.text: Every outbound network call MUST set an explicit timeout that is shorter than the caller's own deadline.
statements.title: Explicit timeouts

statements.applies_when: the content adds or configures retry logic, or loops that repeat a remote call.
statements.not_applies_when: No outbound network call is made, configured or described.
statements.text: Retries MUST be bounded in count, MUST use exponential backoff with jitter, and MUST only be applied to idempotent operations or requests carrying an idempotency key.
statements.title: Bounded retries with backoff

statements.applies_when: the content calls a dependency whose result is optional for the response, such as recommendations, reviews or analytics.
statements.not_applies_when: No outbound network call is made, configured or described.
statements.text: A call to a dependency that is not required for the core user flow SHOULD have a fallback (cached value, default, or feature disabled) instead of failing the request.
statements.title: Degradation for optional dependencies

statements.applies_when: the content is a design that adds a call to a new service, database or third party.
statements.not_applies_when: No outbound network call is made, configured or described.
statements.text: A design that adds a new synchronous dependency MUST state its expected latency, its timeout, and the behavior of the system when the dependency is down.
statements.title: Dependencies in designs

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a tsconfig file.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not TypeScript source code.
statements.text: Projects MUST compile with `"strict": true` in `tsconfig.json`.
statements.title: Strict compiler mode

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes an exported function, class, interface or type.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not TypeScript source code.
statements.text: Exported functions, classes and types MUST NOT use `any` in their public signatures; use `unknown` or a precise type instead.
statements.title: No `any` in exported signatures

statements.applies_when: the content calls an async function or creates a promise.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not TypeScript source code.
statements.text: A promise MUST be awaited, returned, or explicitly handled with `.catch`; it MUST NOT be created and silently dropped.
statements.title: No floating promises

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a try/catch block or a `.catch` handler.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not TypeScript source code.
statements.text: Code in a `catch` block SHOULD treat the error as `unknown` and narrow it (for example with `instanceof`) before reading its properties.
statements.title: Narrow caught errors

statements.applies_when: the content adds a migration that drops, renames or changes the type of a column or table.
statements.not_applies_when: No database schema or migration is involved.
statements.text: Each migration MUST be compatible with the previous version of the application code; a breaking change is split into expand, migrate and contract steps deployed separately.
statements.title: Backward-compatible steps

statements.applies_when: the content adds a column to an existing table.
statements.not_applies_when: No database schema or migration is involved.
statements.text: A column added to an existing table MUST be nullable or have a default value.
statements.title: New columns are nullable or defaulted

statements.applies_when: the content creates an index, rewrites a table, or updates many rows in a migration.
statements.not_applies_when: No database schema or migration is involved.
statements.text: Migrations on large tables MUST NOT take locks that block writes for long periods; indexes are created concurrently and data backfills run in batches outside the migration.
statements.title: No long locks on large tables

statements.applies_when: the content adds a migration file.
statements.not_applies_when: No database schema or migration is involved.
statements.text: Migrations SHOULD provide a down step, or state in a comment why the change cannot be reversed.
statements.title: Reversible migrations

statements.applies_when: the content is a design spec.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is code, a diff, an incident report or a document that does not propose a system design.
statements.text: A spec MUST state the problem, who has it and why it matters now, before it describes the solution.
statements.title: Problem before solution

statements.applies_when: the content is a design spec.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is code, a diff, an incident report or a document that does not propose a system design.
statements.text: A spec MUST list explicit non-goals.
statements.title: Non-goals

statements.applies_when: the content is a design spec.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is code, a diff, an incident report or a document that does not propose a system design.
statements.text: A spec MUST describe at least one alternative that was considered and why it was not chosen.
statements.title: Alternatives considered

statements.applies_when: the content is a design spec for a change that reaches production.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is code, a diff, an incident report or a document that does not propose a system design.
statements.text: A spec MUST describe how the change is rolled out to production and how it is rolled back if it misbehaves.
statements.title: Rollout and rollback

statements.applies_when: the content is a design spec for a service, job or pipeline that runs in production.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is code, a diff, an incident report or a document that does not propose a system design.
statements.text: A spec SHOULD define how success and failure are observed: key metrics, alerts, and service level objectives where relevant.
statements.title: Operability

statements.applies_when: the content is a design spec.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is code, a diff, an incident report or a document that does not propose a system design.
statements.text: A spec MUST describe what personal or sensitive data the system handles and how access to it is controlled, or state that it handles none.
statements.title: Security and privacy

statements.applies_when: the content changes the behavior of search, booking, payment or login flows.
statements.not_applies_when: No feature flag is involved and no user-visible production behavior changes.
statements.text: A change to a critical user flow (search, booking, payment, login) SHOULD be released behind a feature flag that can be turned off without a deploy.
statements.title: Risky changes behind a flag

statements.applies_when: the content defines a new feature flag.
statements.not_applies_when: No feature flag is involved and no user-visible production behavior changes.
statements.text: Every new feature flag MUST declare an owning team and an expiry date in its definition.
statements.title: Owner and expiry

statements.applies_when: the content reads the value of a feature flag.
statements.not_applies_when: No feature flag is involved and no user-visible production behavior changes.
statements.text: Code that reads a flag MUST behave safely when the flag service is unavailable, using the old behavior as the default value.
statements.title: Safe default

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a public Python function or method.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Python source code.
statements.text: Public functions and methods in Python modules SHOULD have type hints for all parameters and the return value.
statements.title: Typed public functions
